title: See your supply chain: list, trace, rank and specify

say: See your supply chain: list, trace, rank and specify.
This is the video for module one of Supply Chain and Raw Materials Sourcing.
A supply chain is every step a material passes through before it becomes your product: farm or factory, wholesaler, trader, transport, and your store.
Once customers depend on you, a missing material becomes a broken promise.

say: A bill of materials, or BOM, lists every input for one batch, with quantity and cost.
Amaka makes zobo in batches of 100 bottles. Her prices are illustrative and approximate.

say: Dried hibiscus costs about 4,500 naira, sugar 7,200, and fresh ginger 1,000.

say: 100 bottles with caps cost about 6,000 naira, and 100 labels 2,500.

say: That is 21,200 naira per batch, or 212 naira per bottle.
Sugar and bottles together are about 62% of her material cost, so a problem with either one hits her harder than a problem with ginger.

say: Tier 3 may be the farm or the factory. You rarely control them, but a problem there reaches you days or weeks later.
So ask your trader where it comes from. Amaka learned her bottles come from one distributor of a single factory.

say: A material is critical if you cannot produce without it and cannot quickly swap it. Ask three questions. Can I make the product without it?

panel.heading: Is this material critical?
items: Can I make the product without it?
Can I switch source within one week?
Circle any branch with only one supplier

say: Can I switch to another source within one week? Amaka cannot: her labels and caps fit only her bottle.

panel.heading: Is this material critical?
items: Can I make the product without it?

Circle any branch with only one supplier

say: Would customers notice a change? If yes, a substitute carries quality risk.

say: One supplier whose absence would stop production is a single point of failure. If only your printer holds your label design, the fix is free: keep your own copy and share it with a second printer.

say: First rank materials by yearly spend. This is ABC analysis. In Bisi's uniform workshop, two fabrics out of eight materials carry 75% of her spend.
Then add supply risk, using the Kraljic matrix.

panel.heading: Four boxes for your materials
items: Bottleneck: extra stock or second source

say: Strategic items have big spend and few good sources, like Bisi's school-colour check fabric. Build a close relationship, and approve a backup before a crisis.

panel.heading: Four boxes for your materials
items: Bottleneck: extra stock or second source

say: Leverage items have big spend but many suppliers, like white shirting. Compare quotes and negotiate.

panel.heading: Four boxes for your materials
items: Bottleneck: extra stock or second source

say: Bottleneck items are cheap but hard to get, like zips in the one colour the school demands. Running out stops delivery, so hold extra stock or find a second source.

panel.heading: Four boxes for your materials
items: Bottleneck: extra stock or second source

say: Non-critical items, like thread, need as little thinking time as possible.

say: Good shea butter means something different to every trader. A specification is a short written description of exactly what you accept.
For example, Funke writes: unrefined shea butter, for cosmetic use.

panel.heading: Write a spec you can actually check

say: Ivory to pale yellow, smooth, no sand or water drops. Mild, nutty smell. Reject if sour or rancid.

panel.heading: Write a spec you can actually check

say: Clean, sealed buckets with the packing date on the lid. And she keeps one 250 g jar from an approved delivery as the standard.

panel.heading: Write a spec you can actually check

say: For a new supplier, she melts and strains 1 kg. The new butter left 100 g of grit, or 10% waste. Her approved supplier's was about 1%.
Use checks you can really do: look, smell, weigh, measure, or a small test batch.

panel.heading: Write a spec you can actually check
panel.rule: Approve a new supplier only after a small trial.

say: If you buy chemicals such as caustic soda or acids, accept only the original sealed, labelled container, with a safety data sheet where possible.
Never accept a chemical in an unlabelled water bottle. Store chemicals away from food and out of children's reach.
Scammers pose as suppliers online. Start with a small trial, pay into an account whose name matches the business, and keep the receipt.

panel.heading: Safe buying rules
items: Ask for a safety data sheet where possible
Store chemicals away from food and children
New supplier: small trial order first
Pay only to an account matching the business

say: To remember. Your bill of materials shows where your money goes. Many shortages start at tier 2 or 3. One supplier is a single point of failure.
Strategic items need a tested backup. And a written spec makes quality checkable.
